thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: High tail latency detected for hosted streaming endpoint /v1/stream in us-west-2. p95=800ms, p99=2.8s (SLO p99=1.5s). Spike started ~2025-03-12T11:03:00Z. Possible noisy neighbor / GPU contention. Paging on-call.

oncall-bot: Paging @alex (oncall) — please acknowledge.

alex (oncall): ack — I’m on it. Moving to #incident-war-room. First pass: are there any deploys? @sven any deploys around 11:00 UTC?

sven: no deploys on the inference fleet at 11:00. I’m pulling metrics now. Quick checks show GPU util ~97% on nodes in gpu-pool-3 and sustained kernel IO wait spikes on one node (gpu-node-42).

maria: I’m seeing a single tenant with a huge increase in batch jobs starting 10:58: tenant=batch-ingest-7. Their job has many short-lived pods with heavy tokenization IO (lots of small file reads). Could be the noisy neighbor.

dana: copying useful cmds:
```
# list pods using a lot of gpu on that node
kubectl get pods -A -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-42
kubectl top pod -A --containers | grep -E "gpu|nvidia"
nvidia-smi -i 0 --query-compute-apps=pid,used_gpu_memory --format=csv
```

sven: ran those — found pod batch-ingest-7-xxxxx using ~80% GPU memory and constantly hitting local disk for preprocessing. Also saw cgroup blkio throttling warnings in dmesg.

alex (oncall): immediate mitigation options — (1) throttle or evict the noisy job, (2) cordon + move latency-sensitive pods off the node, (3) scale up dedicated gpu pool to absorb load. Thoughts?

ryan: +1 to quick eviction of the offending pods, then scale up. We should avoid full node restart if possible. I can patch the autoscaler to add 1 GPU to dedicated pool (will take ~3-4 min to boot).

maria: eviction command I used before:
```
kubectl delete pod batch-ingest-7-xxxxx -n workloads --grace-period=10 --timeout=60s
# or safer: kubectl evict via eviction API
kubectl evict pod batch-ingest-7-xxxxx -n workloads --force
```

alex (oncall): proceeding to evict the top offenders now. I'll annotate customer-impact for follow-up. @ops-bot, please start a temporary taint on gpu-node-42 so scheduler doesn't place new latency-sensitive pods there.

ops-bot: Taint applied: kubernetes.io/not-ready=contended:NoSchedule on node gpu-node-42

sven: eviction in progress. Also adjusted cgroup blkio weight for that pod's slice as a soft throttle while eviction completes:
```
echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<container-id>/blkio.weight
```
(we should capture container-id from docker/pod info)

dana: watching metrics — p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.7s after first evictions. p95 stable around 700-800ms.

ryan: autoscaler request submitted, adding 1x A10x GPU node to gpu-pool-3. ETA ~180s.

maria: found two customer-facing endpoints that experienced visible stalls: Acme Chat (support #4312) and Zephyr Analytics (internal alert). Both hit streaming timeouts. We should notify CS.

alex (oncall): sending quick status to CS and Product now. Short note:
"Brief: high tail latency on streaming in us-west-2 caused by noisy tenant batch-ingest-7. Mitigation: evicted offending pods, tainted node, scaling up pool. p99 improving; customers impacted: Acme Chat, Zephyr Analytics. Follow-ups: rate-limit per-tenant, scheduler QoS, runbook update."

kelly: taking over on-call at 12:00 UTC. Alex handing off current actions.

alex (oncall): handoff: node tainted, top noisy pods evicted, autoscaler requested. Monitoring metrics and logs. Expected next: new node in ~3m, then migrate some latency-sensitive pods to new node to relieve pressure. If p99 stays >1.5s after new node, escalate to P1 and consider rolling restart of gpu-node-42.

ops-bot: new node gpu-node-47 joined cluster and labeled gpu-pool-3 after 190s.

sven: moving a few critical streaming pods to the new node via pod disruption budget bypass:
```
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl uncordon gpu-node-47
```

dana: after migration p99 is now 1.1s, p95 620ms. No streaming stalls reported in the last 2m.

maria: confirmed customer-facing timeouts resolved. CS notified that issue resolved and we’ll follow up with RCA.

ryan: temporary mitigation checklist:
- Per-tenant GPU job cap (hard) — follow-up
- Disabled batch-ingest-7 autoscaling policy to prevent future bursts
- Add blkio/cgroup limits for preprocessing containers
- Improve node-level alerts for sustained IO wait

alex (oncall): filing incident ticket and assigning postmortem owners: sven (infra), maria (ml infra), ryan (autoscaler). Severity set to P2 (SLO breached but self-mitigated within 20m). Customer outreach: CS to send empathetic update and offer credits if needed.

kelly: taking over monitoring. If anything reappears ping me. Nice run, team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved (monitoring). Duration 00:22:47. Summary: noisy tenant causing GPU/IO contention -> evicted pods + scale-up -> p99 restored below SLO. Follow-ups created: INC-2025-045 (rate-limit), INC-2025-046 (runbook), INC-2025-047 (scheduler QoS).
